The total page calculation uses floor(user_count / limit) + 1 rather than rounding up. With 50 members and a limit of 50, it reports two pages and enables Next, which requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. Use a ceiling calculation while retaining the zero-member handling.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: when the total equals a multiple of the limit, the last page is empty (2/2 with no members, offset == total). The golden comment points at the next-offset capping and the candidate points at the page count calculation, but the symptom and root issue are the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Page count includes an extra empty page for exact multiples

The total page calculation uses floor(user_count / limit) + 1 rather than rounding up. With 50 members and a limit of 50, it reports two pages and enables Next, which requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. Use a ceiling calculation while retaining the zero-member handling.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: floor(count/limit)+1 adds an extra empty page when the count is an exact multiple of the limit. The candidate also suggests the correct fix, a ceiling calculation.

false_positives.candidate:
Public member list is truncated without a way to load remaining members

The public group-members route now calls findMembers(), which requests only 50 members by default, but the public members template has no pagination or load-more controls. Non-automatic groups previously returned all members; groups with more than 50 members now have members that cannot be viewed from this page. Add public pagination or otherwise load the remaining results.

Existing membership PATCH requests now silently hide groups

The resources route still accepts PATCH /admin/groups/:id, but update no longer handles the previously supported changes.add and changes.delete payloads. An existing client sending a membership-only PATCH now receives success without changing membership, and because its request omits visible, this assignment also sets the group's visibility to false. Preserve the PATCH contract or explicitly reject obsolete payloads without modifying the group.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update match statistics atomically

The match counter is incremented with an unlocked read-modify-save sequence. If two registration requests match the same blocked email concurrently, both can read the same match_count and save the same incremented value, losing one match. A delayed save can also overwrite a newer last_match_at. Use an atomic database increment/update or lock the record while updating these statistics.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment's main concern is that a predicate/read method has side effects (it updates statistics), which also creates race conditions and makes the name misleading. The candidate covers the race condition in the statistics update inside that same method, but not the side-effect-in-a-read-method design concern. The two overlap on the same code and on the race condition aspect, so this is a partial match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize email addresses before storing and matching blocks

BlockedEmail stores the supplied email unchanged and matches it using an exact, case-sensitive equality query. An entry for `bad@example.com` therefore does not match `bad@EXAMPLE.COM`, although those addresses refer to the same mailbox (domain names are case-insensitive). No normalization is performed by this model or the new validator, so differently cased block entries or registration addresses can evade the block. Normalize both stored entries and lookup values consistently with the application's email handling.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same flaw: BlockedEmail does a case-sensitive exact-match lookup, so a differently cased address can get past the block. The candidate's fix is to normalize the stored entries and the lookup value.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Include alignment for the Mozilla box fallback

The flexbox mixins explicitly support older Firefox through `display: -moz-box` and `display: -moz-inline-box`, but `align-items` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align` property. Firefox versions using that fallback ignore the other alignment declarations, so the newly converted header and small-action rows use the default stretch alignment instead of centering their children, and bullet badges do not receive baseline alignment. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` so the advertised fallback preserves the intended layout.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Apply the untrusted-field restriction to website_name

The new website_name attribute is not included in untrusted_attributes, so it is serialized even when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) suppresses website for a TL0 user viewed anonymously. This exposes the restricted website host (and, for matching domains, its path), and the updated template displays it despite the website field being hidden. Give website_name the same restriction as website and test with a populated TL0 website.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed imports persist unsanitized HTML as cooked posts

TopicEmbed.import passes externally supplied contents through Nokogiri parsing and then stores them using raw_html cooking, which returns the HTML unchanged. Nokogiri::HTML.fragment does not sanitize scripts, event handlers, or javascript URLs. PollFeed calls this method directly with feed content, so malicious feed HTML becomes stored XSS on the forum and in the embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute, and URL-scheme policy before storing it; the appended source URL also needs proper HTML escaping.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment names two issues: a NoMethodError when contents is nil, and XSS from unescaped url interpolation. The candidate's main point is unsanitized content leading to XSS, which is a broader concern. However, it also says the appended source URL needs proper HTML escaping, which covers the XSS half of the golden comment. It does not mention the nil problem. That is a partial match on the same code issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB closing statement prevents rendering existing discussions

The template closes its conditional with `end if` without a condition after `if`. This is invalid Ruby syntax, so compiling the ERB raises a SyntaxError whenever the controller renders an existing embedded topic. Replace it with `end` and add a controller test that actually renders the view.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same problem: the ERB block is closed with an invalid `end if` that raises at render time, and both say to replace it with `end`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RSS items without a content element abort feed polling

The poller unconditionally calls scrub on i.content. RSS feeds commonly supply article text in description rather than content:encoded, leaving content nil; such an item raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire polling job before subsequent items are imported. Select the appropriate content/description field with a nil-safe fallback and test polling an actual RSS feed with description-only items.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. Calling scrub on a nil i.content raises an error for RSS items that lack content, and both propose falling back to description.

false_positives.candidate:
Redirects bypass the remote retrieval host restriction

TopicRetriever checks only the host of the initial embed URL, then import_remote fetches it with open-uri, which follows HTTP redirects. An endpoint on the configured embedding host can therefore redirect the worker to an internal HTTP service or another unapproved host, and the fetched content can be published as a topic. Validate each redirect destination and reject private/internal addresses before fetching, rather than relying solely on the initial URI host check.

Relative and protocol-relative article URLs are resolved incorrectly

absolutize_urls only handles values starting with `/` and treats all of them as paths on the article host. Consequently `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, while document-relative values such as `images/image.jpg` remain relative to the Discourse page instead of the source article. Both links and images in imported articles can therefore break or point to the wrong site. Resolve href and src values against the full source URI using URI joining, preserving protocol-relative hosts.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this second `self.downsize` definition replaces the definition accepting `max_width, max_height, opts`. Existing callers passing width and height now either raise ArgumentError (when also passing options) or pass the height as `opts`, causing `optimize` to fail when it accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve a single method that supports both calling conventions, or give the dimensions-string variant a different name.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same bug. The second downsize definition overrides the first one, which took max_width and max_height, and this breaks existing callers that pass width and height separately.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The fixed size limit also overrides attachment upload settings

`validateUploadedFile` validates both images and attachments, but the new unconditional 10 MB limit replaces `max_attachment_size_kb` as well as the image limit. Attachments cannot benefit from the new image downsizing: sites permitting attachments larger than 10 MB now have valid uploads blocked in the browser, while sites with smaller attachment limits unnecessarily accept files for upload that the server will reject. Apply the relaxed limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the hardcoded 10MB limit ignores the per-type configured size settings, so the client-side limit diverges from the server-side one. The candidate focuses on the attachment setting, but that is one instance of the same per-type settings problem the golden comment describes.

false_positives.candidate:
Large animated GIF uploads lose their animation even when allowed

The resize call passes the temporary file's path rather than a path with the original filename's extension. `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects its animated implementation when the source path ends in `.gif`, but multipart upload temporary paths normally have no such extension. Consequently, even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, a large animated GIF goes through the `convert` instructions using `[0]` and is permanently replaced by its first frame. Detect animation/image type independently of the temporary path before modifying the original upload.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle users without an existing TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the action unconditionally reads tu.notification_level. The URL is not tied to the email recipient, so a user opening a forwarded email or opening it while logged into another account can have access to the topic without having a TopicUser row. That valid request raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of allowing the user to unsubscribe. Create or update the preference through TopicUser.change, which supports missing records.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point out that TopicUser.find_by can return nil and that calling methods on tu then crashes. This is the same nil pointer issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not change notification preferences through an authenticated GET

The new GET route invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a lower notification level for the currently logged-in user. GET requests are not protected by Rails' CSRF token verification, and the action also skips the XHR check. An external site can therefore navigate a logged-in user to this URL and disable their topic notifications without consent. Serve the preference page on GET and perform the mutation through a CSRF-protected POST.

Record the unsubscribe as an explicit user preference change

Saving notification_level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged, unlike TopicUser.change, which records the user_changed reason. For automatically tracked topics whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read automatically sets the level back to tracking once the reading-time threshold is reached. Consequently, a subsequent visit can undo the unsubscribe. Use the normal notification-change mechanism so the explicit preference is preserved.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendar queries after deleting cached data

The delete-cache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The wrapper passes props.onChanged directly, which is optional and does not itself refresh the wrapper's query, and that query disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Consequently, a successful deletion can leave the old cache timestamp and Delete cached data action visible even though the cache no longer exists. Invalidate the connected-calendar queries on success, as the disconnect mutation already does, so all scopes display the updated cache status.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Override validation accepts slots only partially inside availability

The override checks reject slots ending at or before the override start and slots starting after its end, but do not require the whole slot to fit inside the override. For example, a fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 slot generated by a round-robin host. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes. Require slotStartTime >= override start and slotEndTime <= override end for at least one override interval.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment says the end-boundary check wrongly uses slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. The candidate flags the same check: it only rejects slots that start after the override end, and it proposes requiring slotEndTime <= override end. That is the same underlying bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts

When a slot's date has an override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking the host's busy times. An override defines working availability, not an exemption from existing bookings or calendar conflicts. Consequently, both fixed and round-robin hosts can be shown as available during an existing meeting on an override date. Validate the override window and then continue through the busy-time checks.

Split working hours reject slots inside valid intervals

The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it fits inside at least one interval. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon interval, and afternoon slots are rejected by the morning interval. This newly added check removes valid availability for ordinary split-day schedules. Check for containment in an applicable interval, using the slot end time rather than the slot start for the end boundary.

Timezone conversion discards date changes at midnight

The converted override boundaries are reduced to hour/minute values without preserving a day rollover, while activeOverrides is still selected using the unconverted override start date. For example, a UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+3 becomes 01:00–02:00 but is inserted into the original attendee date instead of the following date. An interval crossing attendee midnight can also produce startTime > endTime and disappear entirely. Convert the full override interval to attendee time, select it by overlap with the attendee day, and clip or split it at day boundaries before extracting minutes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment the retry counter atomically

Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before processing the batch. If cron invocations overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they write the same value, so two failed attempts are recorded as one and the reminder remains eligible for further attempts instead of reaching the deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` operation in both failure paths.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem. Writing a stale `reminder.retryCount + 1` can lose increments when runs overlap. Both recommend Prisma's atomic `increment` and say the fix applies to both failure paths.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not let failure bookkeeping abort the entire batch

The catch block now awaits a Prisma update without handling errors from that update. If a reminder is deleted while the batch is processing (for example, by an overlapping cleanup invocation), the update throws a record-not-found error out of the catch block. This aborts the cron request and skips every remaining reminder in the batch; previously the scheduling error was logged and processing continued. Handle bookkeeping failures separately, including reminders that no longer exist, so one failed reminder cannot stop the batch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve or migrate the existing findMany API

This replaces the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method with `getBaseConditions()`, but the PR contains no migration of production consumers. These APIs are not interchangeable: `findMany` executed a query, honored selection and other query arguments, and applied authorization and filters, whereas `getBaseConditions` only returns a SQL fragment. Existing callers of `service.findMany(...)` will now fail type checking (or throw at runtime). Update all consumers to execute appropriately authorized raw queries in the same change, or retain a compatible query method until they are migrated.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder

This helper assigns the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the parsed response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office 365 permits refresh_token to be absent and previously retained the existing token when merging the response. The new placeholder overwrites that valid token in the database, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: when the refresh_token is missing from the response, it is replaced with the hardcoded string 'refresh_token'. That invalidates the token and breaks subsequent refreshes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Computed Zod keys do not validate or preserve token expiry fields

Using a Zod schema's toString() as an object key produces a literal key such as "[object Object]", not a dynamic property validator. The two computed keys also collide. Since z.object strips unknown properties, synced responses lose expires_in, expiry_date, and refresh_token instead of preserving them. Consumers such as Zoom then calculate expiry from undefined and cannot persist usable credentials. Define explicit supported fields or a passthrough schema with appropriate expiry validation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same code: the computed keys built from z.string().toString() in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which they agree is broken. They describe the consequence differently. The golden says it throws a runtime error. The candidate says the keys become literal "[object Object]" and the token expiry fields get stripped. The underlying issue is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Persist the parsed token data rather than the safeParse result

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the credentials themselves. Saving this wrapper as credential.key removes access_token and refresh_token from the expected top-level location. After any Google token refresh, even with syncing disabled, subsequent service construction fails googleCredentialSchema validation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the safeParse wrapper is persisted as the credential key when the parsed token data should be stored instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers

The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but the fallback branch returns whatever the provider callback returns. Google and the Zoho integrations read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly from an SDK token object. None of those properties exist on a fetch Response, regardless of the JSON returned by the sync endpoint. Enabling syncing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Parse and normalize the response or adapt each caller to the sync response contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem. In the sync path the code returns a fetch Response, while callers such as Google (res.data) and HubSpot (token object) expect integration-specific shapes, so refreshes break at runtime.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers

The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but the fallback branch returns whatever the provider callback returns. Google and the Zoho integrations read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly from an SDK token object. None of those properties exist on a fetch Response, regardless of the JSON returned by the sync endpoint. Enabling syncing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Parse and normalize the response or adapt each caller to the sync response contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. The sync path returns a fetch Response, which has no .data. Callers that read res.data, such as Google, therefore break, because the return shape of refreshOAuthTokens is inconsistent.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass the user ID rather than the credential ID to token syncing

The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID, but Bigin passes credentialId. The helper sends that value as calcomUserId to the parent platform, requesting tokens for the wrong user whenever these IDs differ. This can fail refreshes or associate another user's tokens with this credential. Carry credential.userId through to this call; team credentials should retain the provider fallback.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: refreshOAuthTokens receives credentialId when it should receive userId, so the lookup and sync go to the wrong user.

false_positives.candidate:
Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh

The new getClient implementation calls prisma.credential.update, but this file does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and throws ReferenceError at runtime after a successful token request, preventing Salesforce client initialization and event operations.

Use the installed Zoom app slug in sync requests

The refresh request sends appSlug "zoomvideo", but Zoom credentials and the callback use the app ID/slug "zoom". A parent app store resolving the supplied appSlug against the same slugs used by the credential webhook cannot find this integration. Send "zoom" so refresh and credential creation identify the same app.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await reminder cancellation database operations before returning

The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled-state update themselves, but their promises are discarded inside forEach. Previously the reminder database deletions were included in the awaited Promise.all. The handler can now return successfully before cancellation is persisted, and a serverless request may finish before these operations complete, leaving reminders active. Collect and await both email and SMS helper promises; the same issue occurs in the changed requestReschedule handler.

The candidate also points to the reschedule handler, which matches the golden comment's scope.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron

Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking five minutes before its reminder sends leaves the email scheduled at SendGrid until after delivery. The cron also deletes past reminders before processing cancellations, so it then discards this cancellation entirely. Reminders close to their send time need an immediate cancellation path.

Reschedules still bypass the pending-cancellation limit workaround

Every rescheduled booking passes immediateDelete=true, which immediately creates a SendGrid pending cancellation regardless of how far away the reminder is. This retains the 100-pending-cancellations failure described by this PR for reschedules. Furthermore, that branch catches API errors without marking the reminder cancelled, so when the limit is reached the cron cannot retry and the old booking's reminder is still sent. Reschedules should use deferred cancellation with a persisted retry state, except when immediate cancellation is necessary.

Persist successful cancellations before another request can fail

The cancellation loop accumulates lazy Prisma delete promises and executes them only after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any request fails, execution jumps to the catch and none of the successfully cancelled reminders are deleted. Subsequent cron runs therefore submit those same batch IDs again; an already-cancelled batch can fail and repeatedly prevent later reminders from being processed. Persist each successful cancellation and handle errors per reminder so one failed request cannot block the rest of the queue.

This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

Combine these checks with OR to implement the intended admin-or-owner permission.

A direct mutation with the same email twice therefore passes both entries to createMany, creating duplicate attendees or failing on a database uniqueness constraint. true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Backup-code verification reads the encrypted array and then overwrites it using an unconditional update by user ID. Two simultaneous login requests can read the same unused code, both validate it, and both successfully authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic compare-and-swap with retry or a suitably serialized transaction, and only authenticate after successfully consuming the code.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process type check

Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this check is false for production workers and a hung worker is never killed before its replacement starts. The old and replacement workers can then flush the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate production and accumulating stuck processes. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from processes instead.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same root cause: spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess instances, so the multiprocessing.Process isinstance check fails and hung workers are not killed. Extra details about join() and duplicate flushing do not change the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

When the shared join deadline expires, this loop breaks before cleaning up the remaining workers. If the first worker consumes the timeout, all later workers are left running, potentially blocked in Redis or Kafka calls despite the stopped flag. During rebalancing the new strategy can start replacement flushers while these old workers still own the same shards. The deadline should limit waiting, not skip termination of the remaining processes.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: breaking out of the worker-join loop when the shared deadline expires skips termination of remaining flushers, leaving them running. The candidate's extra details are consistent with that concern.

The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this second `self.downsize` definition replaces the definition accepting `max_width, max_height, opts`. Existing callers passing width and height now either raise ArgumentError (when also passing options) or pass the height as `opts`, causing `optimize` to fail when it accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve a single method that supports both calling conventions, or give the dimensions-string variant a different name.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same Ruby method-redefinition bug: a second self.downsize definition overrides the earlier max_width/max_height version because Ruby does not overload by signature, breaking existing callers. The candidate adds consequences and a fix suggestion, but the underlying issue matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

`validateUploadedFile` validates both images and attachments, but the new unconditional 10 MB limit replaces `max_attachment_size_kb` as well as the image limit. Apply the relaxed limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: a hardcoded client-side size limit ignores configured per-type max_*_size_kb settings, causing client/server divergence for images and attachments.

false_positives.candidate:
Large animated GIF uploads lose their animation even when allowed

The resize call passes the temporary file's path rather than a path with the original filename's extension. `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects its animated implementation when the source path ends in `.gif`, but multipart upload temporary paths normally have no such extension. Consequently, even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, a large animated GIF goes through the `convert` instructions using `[0]` and is permanently replaced by its first frame. Detect animation/image type independently of the temporary path before modifying the original upload.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:

TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the action unconditionally reads tu.notification_level. The URL is not tied to the email recipient, so a user opening a forwarded email or opening it while logged into another account can have access to the topic without having a TopicUser row. That valid request raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of allowing the user to unsubscribe. Create or update the preference through TopicUser.change, which supports missing records.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: TopicUser.find_by may return nil, and unconditionally calling notification_level on it raises NoMethodError. The candidate adds context and a fix, but the underlying issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not change notification preferences through an authenticated GET

The new GET route invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a lower notification level for the currently logged-in user. GET requests are not protected by Rails' CSRF token verification, and the action also skips the XHR check. An external site can therefore navigate a logged-in user to this URL and disable their topic notifications without consent. Serve the preference page on GET and perform the mutation through a CSRF-protected POST.

Record the unsubscribe as an explicit user preference change

Saving notification_level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged, unlike TopicUser.change, which records the user_changed reason. For automatically tracked topics whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read automatically sets the level back to tracking once the reading-time threshold is reached. Consequently, a subsequent visit can undo the unsubscribe. Use the normal notification-change mechanism so the explicit preference is preserved.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendar queries after deleting cached data

This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Split working hours reject slots inside valid intervals

The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it fits inside at least one interval. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon interval, and afternoon slots are rejected by the morning interval. This newly added check removes valid availability for ordinary split-day schedules. Check for containment in an applicable interval, using the slot end time rather than the slot start for the end boundary.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same boundary bug: slot containment is evaluated with the slot start time instead of the slot end time, causing valid slots to be rejected. The split-hours explanation is additional context around that same issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts

When a slot's date has an override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking the host's busy times. An override defines working availability, not an exemption from existing bookings or calendar conflicts. Consequently, both fixed and round-robin hosts can be shown as available during an existing meeting on an override date. Validate the override window and then continue through the busy-time checks.

Timezone conversion discards date changes at midnight

The converted override boundaries are reduced to hour/minute values without preserving a day rollover, while activeOverrides is still selected using the unconverted override start date. For example, a UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+3 becomes 01:00–02:00 but is inserted into the original attendee date instead of the following date. An interval crossing attendee midnight can also produce startTime > endTime and disappear entirely. Convert the full override interval to attendee time, select it by overlap with the attendee day, and clip or split it at day boundaries before extracting minutes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment the retry counter atomically

Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before processing the batch. If cron invocations overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they write the same value, so two failed attempts are recorded as one and the reminder remains eligible for further attempts instead of reaching the deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` operation in both failure paths.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same race condition: failure paths compute reminder.retryCount + 1 from a stale pre-read value, so concurrent failures can overwrite the same count and miss the deletion threshold. Both recommend Prisma's atomic increment in both failure paths.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not let failure bookkeeping abort the entire batch

The catch block now awaits a Prisma update without handling errors from that update. If a reminder is deleted while the batch is processing (for example, by an overlapping cleanup invocation), the update throws a record-not-found error out of the catch block. This aborts the cron request and skips every remaining reminder in the batch; previously the scheduling error was logged and processing continued. Handle bookkeeping failures separately, including reminders that no longer exist, so one failed reminder cannot stop the batch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve or migrate the existing findMany API

This replaces the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method with `getBaseConditions()`, but the PR contains no migration of production consumers. These APIs are not interchangeable: `findMany` executed a query, honored selection and other query arguments, and applied authorization and filters, whereas `getBaseConditions` only returns a SQL fragment. Existing callers of `service.findMany(...)` will now fail type checking (or throw at runtime). Update all consumers to execute appropriately authorized raw queries in the same change, or retain a compatible query method until they are migrated.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

This helper assigns the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the parsed response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. The new placeholder overwrites that valid token in the database, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: when an OAuth refresh response omits refresh_token, the code substitutes the literal string 'refresh_token', overwriting the existing valid token and causing subsequent refreshes to fail. The candidate adds provider context but points to the same root cause and fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

Since z.object strips unknown properties, synced responses lose expires_in, expiry_date, and refresh_token instead of preserving them. Consumers such as Zoom then calculate expiry from undefined and cannot persist usable credentials. Define explicit supported fields or a passthrough schema with appropriate expiry validation.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: computed keys built from Zod schema toString() are invalid and do not validate/preserve expiry fields. It elaborates on the runtime consequences, but the underlying issue matches the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

Saving this wrapper as credential.key removes access_token and refresh_token from the expected top-level location. After any Google token refresh, even with syncing disabled, subsequent service construction fails googleCredentialSchema validation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify that the safeParse wrapper is persisted instead of its parsed credential data, causing token fields to be stored in the wrong shape and later validation to fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

None of those properties exist on a fetch Response, regardless of the JSON returned by the sync endpoint. Enabling syncing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Parse and normalize the response or adapt each caller to the sync response contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same contract mismatch: the credential-sync path returns a fetch Response, while provider refresh callers expect integration-specific token objects or response.data, causing runtime failures when sync is enabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID, but Bigin passes credentialId. The helper sends that value as calcomUserId to the parent platform, requesting tokens for the wrong user whenever these IDs differ. This can fail refreshes or associate another user's tokens with this credential. Carry credential.userId through to this call; team credentials should retain the provider fallback.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId instead of the Cal.com userId, causing token sync/refresh to target the wrong user. The candidate describes the same root cause and impact, with additional fix guidance.

false_positives.candidate:
Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh

The new getClient implementation calls prisma.credential.update, but this file does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and throws ReferenceError at runtime after a successful token request, preventing Salesforce client initialization and event operations.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. Await reminder cancellation database operations before returning

The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled-state update themselves, but their promises are discarded inside forEach. Previously the reminder database deletions were included in the awaited Promise.all. The handler can now return successfully before cancellation is persisted, and a serverless request may finish before these operations complete, leaving reminders active. The candidate's focus on requestReschedule and changed handlers is a semantic match for the golden locations.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedules still bypass the pending-cancellation limit workaround

Every rescheduled booking passes immediateDelete=true, which immediately creates a SendGrid pending cancellation regardless of how far away the reminder is. This retains the 100-pending-cancellations failure described by this PR for reschedules. Furthermore, that branch catches API errors without marking the reminder cancelled, so when the limit is reached the cron cannot retry and the old booking's reminder is still sent. Reschedules should use deferred cancellation with a persisted retry state, except when immediate cancellation is necessary.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments target the immediateDelete=true path in deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its failure to update the WorkflowReminder database state. The candidate notes the branch catches API errors without marking the reminder cancelled (leaving the old reminder active), which aligns with the golden comment's core concern that the DB record is not properly cleaned up or marked cancelled in this path.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron

Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking five minutes before its reminder sends leaves the email scheduled at SendGrid until after delivery. The cron also deletes past reminders before processing cancellations, so it then discards this cancellation entirely. Reminders close to their send time need an immediate cancellation path.

Persist successful cancellations before another request can fail

The cancellation loop accumulates lazy Prisma delete promises and executes them only after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any request fails, execution jumps to the catch and none of the successfully cancelled reminders are deleted. Subsequent cron runs therefore submit those same batch IDs again; an already-cancelled batch can fail and repeatedly prevent later reminders from being processed. Persist each successful cancellation and handle errors per reminder so one failed request cannot block the rest of the queue.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without lowercasing. A blacklisted address submitted with uppercase characters passes this filter and receives an invitation. Normalize incoming addresses before blacklist comparison and persistence.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same blacklist bypass: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so uppercase variants pass the check.

Use OR for team admin or owner authorization

Admin and owner are distinct membership roles, so a team administrator or owner who is not also the booking organizer or an attendee is denied permission to add guests. Combine these checks with OR to implement the intended admin-or-owner permission.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Deduplicate incoming guests on the server

uniqueGuests only filters against existing booking attendees; it does not remove duplicates within the incoming guests array, and the server schema accepts duplicate addresses. A direct mutation with the same email twice therefore passes both entries to createMany, creating duplicate attendees or failing on a database uniqueness constraint. The dialog's client-side refinement does not protect this endpoint; validate or deduplicate the request on the server.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: uniqueGuests only filters existing/blacklisted attendees and does not deduplicate repeated emails within the incoming guests array, allowing createMany to insert duplicates or hit a uniqueness constraint. The candidate adds that server-side validation is needed, which is consistent with the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee, unlike the other booking notification functions which respect eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Consequently, adding guests sends standard emails even for event types configured to disable them, including existing attendees who should receive no standard notifications. Pass the event type metadata through the handler and apply the same suppression checks here.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: sendAddGuestsEmails fails to honor event-type standard email disable flags, so host/attendee emails are sent even when disabled. The candidate names the specific flags and suggests the same suppression checks.

false_positives.candidate:

The handler permits attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's. When an attendee adds a guest, the calendar reference belongs to the organizer and cannot be updated using the attendee's calendar credentials. false_negatives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Consume backup codes atomically to enforce single use

Backup-code verification reads the encrypted array and then overwrites it using an unconditional update by user ID. Two simultaneous login requests can read the same unused code, both validate it, and both successfully authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic compare-and-swap with retry or a suitably serialized transaction, and only authenticate after successfully consuming the code.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race condition in backup-code verification: concurrent requests can read the same unused code, both pass validation, and both authenticate before the update is persisted, violating one-time-use semantics. The candidate's additional lost-update concern does not change the core issue.

false_positives.candidate:

The new backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code regardless of whether a supplied totpCode is valid. Earlier password verification is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. An attacker can therefore submit a valid backup code together with an arbitrary totpCode (for example, "x") and authenticate to a password-based account without knowing its password; the TOTP is never checked because the backup-code branch takes precedence. Ensure password verification cannot be bypassed by an unverified field when authenticating with a backup code.

Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.

Guard the missing destination calendar in the Meet fallback

When an event uses Google Meet but has no destination calendar, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar and accessing its integration throws. true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same null-reference bug: destructuring a missing/null destinationCalendar yields undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar, and subsequent integration access throws instead of allowing the Meet fallback.

Each destination's credential is used to create an event, but every adapter receives the full destination array. true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same calendar-selection bug: the code fails to choose the destination/calendar belonging to the current credential and instead uses incorrect matching logic. Both recommend selecting by credential ID (or otherwise scoping to the current destination).

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:

false_positives.candidate:

A collective event whose main host has no calendar but whose other hosts have connected calendars consequently creates no calendar events for those hosts. Initialize an empty array before appending the team destinations.

Preserve credential IDs on video references

Restore the destination fallback for legacy Google references

When externalCalendarId is null or absent, the new fallback searches destination calendars for an externalId equal to that missing value, which cannot match a normal calendar ID. Google update requests consequently receive no calendarId and fail for legacy booking references without a stored external calendar ID, even when the event has a valid destination calendar. The analogous delete fallback instead targets primary and can leave events in non-primary calendars undeleted.

Delete recurring instances using each reference's own credential

In the all-remaining-recurring-bookings branch, the fetched credential for the current reference is ignored. The code instead iterates only the organizer's credentials and selects just the first calendar reference from each instance. For the newly supported collective bookings, secondary hosts' calendar events are never deleted, even though every booking is marked cancelled. Iterate the references of each updated booking and resolve their matching credentials.

Await the async reschedule cleanup callbacks

The new async callback is passed to forEach, which discards its returned promise. In particular, failures while importing or constructing the calendar in getCalendar now become rejected promises that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch; previously synchronous calendar-construction errors were caught there. Reschedule can report success with cleanup still running or failed, and these failures can produce unhandled rejections. Await a mapped Promise.all (or use an awaited loop) inside the try/catch. The same change is needed in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Defer dynamic imports until the corresponding app is requested

Each import() is executed immediately when the app-store registry is evaluated, so importing the registry still starts loading and evaluating every app, including apps unused by the request. This does not provide on-demand loading and adds concurrent chunk loading to cold starts. Store loader functions and invoke only the selected loader instead. It also avoids leaving rejected imports for unused apps without a rejection handler.
